parts.text: In this experiment, you will investigate the forces supporting a metre rule. Carry out the following instructions, referring to Fig. 1.1. Do not attempt to change the position of either newton meter by adjusting the positions of the loops of thread attached to them. Fig. 1.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Move the 1.00 N load to a distance d = 25.0 cm from the 0.0 cm end of the rule. Move one stand slightly, if necessary, so that the newton meters are as near to vertical as possible. Read, and record in Table 1.1, the value F P on newton meter P and the value F Q on newton meter Q. Repeat this procedure for d = 35.0 cm, d = 45.0 cm, d = 55.0 cm and d = 65.0 cm. Table 1.1 d / cm F P / N F Q / N 25.0 35.0 45.0 55.0 65.0 [2]

ms.label: 1(a)
ms.text:
5 FP values decreasing and 5 FQ values increasing
all < 3 N and to ⩾ 1 d.p.

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Plot a graph of F P / N ( y -axis) against d / cm ( x -axis). On the same axes, and using the same scales, plot a graph of F Q / N ( y -axis) against d / cm ( x -axis). Draw two best-fit lines, one for each set of plots. Show clearly on your graph which line is for F P and which line is for F Q . [5] F P / N F Q / N

ms.label: 1(b)
ms.text:
graph:

x-axis labelled with quantity and unit

suitable scales (plots occupying at least 3 large squares in each direction)

plots all correct to ½ small square and precise plots

2 well judged lines and thin lines

intersection at d = 50.0 cm to ±1 small square

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) From your graph, determine F 0 , the value of F P where the two best-fit lines cross. F 0 = ............................................................... Calculate the weight W R of the metre rule, using the equation W R = (2 × F 0 ) – k , where k = 1.00 N. W R = ............................................................... [2]

ms.label: 1(c)
ms.text:
F0 present and WR in range 1 (N) to 3 (N)
WR expressed to 2 or 3 significant figures and with unit of N

ms.label: 1(d)
ms.text:
any valid method e.g.
check equal distance between rule and bench at two places OR
use set square/protractor between stand and rule OR
line up with suitable (named) surface

ms.label: 1(e)
ms.text:
forcemeter Q has zero error OR
has not been set to 0 at start
